knowledge_graph.title: National debt of the Philippines
knowledge_graph.description: The national debt of the Philippines is the total debt, or unpaid borrowed funds, carried by the national government of the Philippines. As of the end of October 2024, the total national debt of the Philippines amounts to ₱15.1889 trillion.

related_questions.question: Which country has the highest debt to GDP ratio?

text_blocks.snippet: In recent years, Sudan has frequently been cited as having the highest debt-to-GDP ratio, with figures reaching 252% in 2023, according to The Indian Express. This high ratio is largely due to prolonged conflict and economic instability. Following Sudan, Japan has the highest debt-to-GDP ratio among developed countries, with figures around 235%.

related_questions.question: What is America's debt to GDP ratio?

text_blocks.snippet: The United States debt-to-GDP ratio is currently around 123%. This means the U.S. federal debt is larger than the nation's total annual economic output (GDP). Specifically, the national debt is approximately $36 trillion, while the GDP is around $29 trillion.

list.title: Debt:
list.snippet: The U.S. national debt is over $36 trillion, according to the U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data.

list.title: GDP:
list.snippet: The U.S. GDP is approximately $29 trillion.

list.title: Ratio:
list.snippet: Dividing the debt by the GDP results in a ratio of roughly 123%, according to the International Monetary Fund.

list.title: Trend:
list.snippet: The debt-to-GDP ratio has been on the rise for several decades, especially during periods of economic downturn and government spending initiatives.

list.title: Significance:
list.snippet: A debt-to-GDP ratio above 100% is generally seen as a warning sign, as it can indicate that the government may have difficulty managing its debt obligations, potentially leading to higher interest rates and economic instability.

text_blocks.snippet: The Philippines' debt-to-GDP ratio is currently around 60%, with recent figures showing a slight decrease from previous years, but still high. Specifically, the debt-to-GDP ratio was reported at 60.7% in December 2024. The government is aiming to reduce this ratio to around 56.3% by 2028, according to the BusinessMirror.

list.snippet: Recent Figures: The debt-to-GDP ratio was 60.7% in December 2024.
Government Target: The government aims to reduce the debt-to-GDP ratio to 56.3% by 2028.
Historical Context: The ratio has fluctuated over time, reaching a high of 74.9% in 1993 and a low of 39.6% in 2019.
Factors Influencing Ratio: The debt-to-GDP ratio is influenced by factors such as economic growth, government spending, and tax revenue.
Economic Growth: The Philippines' GDP is growing, which helps to lower the debt-to-GDP ratio, but government spending and borrowing also play a role.
Government Efforts: The government is focusing on increasing revenue collection and managing its finances to reduce the debt-to-GDP ratio according to ANC.
